title: Box Out Battle
description: A competitive two-player rebounding drill: find your man, make contact, seal, and secure the board against live competition.
goal: Build the habit of finding a body, making contact, and sealing before pursuing the rebound.
setup: Pair up: one offensive rebounder, one defender. Start at the elbows or low blocks.
A coach or third player shoots from the perimeter to start each rep.
First to 5 secured rebounds wins the round; then swap offense and defense.

instructions.title: Find your man on the shot
instructions.detail: The moment the shot goes up, the defender turns, finds the offensive player, and makes forearm contact.

instructions.title: Seal and drive back
instructions.detail: Defender pivots into the offensive player, seals with a wide base, and drives them away from the basket.

instructions.title: Pursue the ball
instructions.detail: After contact, both players go after the rebound — the defender keeps the seal until the ball is secured.

instructions.title: Finish the rep
instructions.detail: Whoever grabs the rebound must chin the ball and make a strong outlet pass before the next rep starts.

instructions.title: Rotate spots
instructions.detail: Move the starting positions around the paint — elbows, blocks, short corner — 5 reps each, then switch roles.

coachingPoints: Contact first, ball second — players who chase the ball without contact get out-rebounded.
Wide base and low hips on the seal; a narrow stance gets pushed under the basket.
Chin the rebound with two hands and elbows out — then outlet, don't dribble into trouble.
The offensive player should practice the counter: swim move, spin, or quick second jump around the seal.
commonMistakes: Watching the shot instead of finding a body — by the time you look, the offensive player is already past you.
Boxing out with arms instead of the body — contact comes from the hips and legs, not a push.
progression: Go 2-on-2 or 3-on-3 with a shot from anywhere, require the offense to tip the ball before securing, or play to 7 with a conditioning penalty for the loser.
regression: Start from a stationary box-out hold (no live rebound), slow the pace, or remove the offensive player and practice seal-and-pursue footwork solo.
gameApplication: Rebounding is effort plus technique — teams that box out consistently end possessions and create the transition chances that win games.
